visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: You invest €100 at 10% a year for two years. What do you have at the end?
questions.explain: In year two you also earn interest on the first year's interest: 100 × 1.1 × 1.1 = 121.
questions.explain_at: That's compounding: you earn returns on your returns

questions.q: What's the present value of €110 received in one year, at a 10% discount rate?
questions.explain: Divide by 1.1; don't subtract 10%. 110 ÷ 1.1 = 100. Subtracting 10% gives 99.
questions.explain_at: Discounting means dividing by one point one

questions.q: The discount rate goes up. What happens to the DCF value?

options.text: It goes up: investors want more
It goes up for growth companies

questions.explain: You divide by a bigger number, so future cash is worth less today. At 15% the café drops from 249 to 228.
questions.explain_at: Third trap, and people say it in interviews all the time

questions.q: Dell went private at $13.75 a share; the judge said $17.62. Roughly what percentage above the deal price is that?
questions.explain: The gap is $3.87; divided by $13.75 that's about 28%. Dividing by $17.62 instead gives 22%.
questions.explain_at: About twenty-eight percent above the deal price

questions.q: You discount unlevered free cash flow at the WACC. What do you get?
questions.explain: Unlevered cash flow at the WACC values the whole business: enterprise value. Subtract net debt to bridge to equity value.
